found_values.value: The owner set over-temperature at 55 °C and under-temperature at 0 °C (2026-09-30). Found for research: per-cell overvoltage on charge at 4.25 V, 24.8 mV above the BQ25723's 4.2252 V a cell regulation maximum (V138), and 50 mV above the pack's 4.2 V full charge. Short circuit: a trip band, with the part's stated tolerance, above the overcurrent band of V284 (60 A) and at or below 180 A, the pack's 60C burst ('Kurzzeitiger Entladestrom: max. 60C (180,0A)'), whose duration the vendor does not state. Per-cell undervoltage is R5's 3.0 V floor (F9)

Yes, up to the input limit, 3.0 A at 5 V (15 W, F8), less the charge current. The BQ25723's NVDC path regulates VSYS at the minimum system voltage when the battery is depleted or removed ('Even with a depleted battery, the system ...', 9.3; BATDRV pin: 'BATFET is in linear mode to regulate VSYS at minimum system voltage when battery is depleted'). The servo supply's 53.3 W is not available from USB-C
found_values.source: https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/bq25723.pdf (SLUSE64, HTTP 200, 4,002,198 bytes), pin 21 BATDRV and the VSYS_MIN section

found_values.value: Yes: USB-C is the only charge source (F8), so a pack at the 3.0 V floor recovers on the bench only if it charges while the floor disconnect is open. The charger need not sit on the cells' side: with the MAX17320G22+ as the protector, 'All discharge-only faults are released when the charger is connected', and the BQ25723 holds VSYS from VBUS so the RP2354B can write ChargeCurrent (reset 0000h). Below VSYS_MIN the charge is clamped to 384 mA. The release of the discharge fault on charger connection also reconnects the pack to the board's load: R5's reconnect condition (IOBoard.md Pack reconnect) has to cover it
found_values.source: https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/MAX17320.pdf (Rev 12, vendors.py fetch --client safari, HTTP 200, 4,371,109 bytes), Ideal-Diode Control; https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/bq25723.pdf 9.6.2 ChargeCurrent and ICLAMP; F8, F9
